headline: Medium pairwise risk: shared file-based workflows can leak or corrupt work, while Botpress’s raw content handling can amplify prompt-injection and Plane’s broad egress can propagate bad outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls, and Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks that could carry attacker-controlled content. Because the pair lacks a documented shared channel, this is inferred rather than proven, but the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Plane file uploads or hyperlinks are forwarded into Botpress prompts without sanitization
IF Botpress treats uploaded content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a manual review step before forwarding Plane content to Botpress
Strip instructions from uploaded files and hyperlinks before ingestion
Use a fixed prompt template that labels Plane content as untrusted
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between systems
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents behind separate workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches files, notes, issues, and hyperlinks and has broad network egress, while Botpress is a support agent with no stated egress and no documented workspace isolation. A shared file or ticket workflow could expose sensitive content from Plane into Botpress outputs, but the exact path is not directly documented.
conditions: IF the same files or notes are copied from Plane into Botpress conversations
IF Botpress is given access to Plane attachments or issue text
mitigations: Limit Botpress inputs to redacted excerpts only
Disable attachment forwarding from Plane to Botpress
Review shared tickets for secrets before handoff
requires-engineering: separate storage for support and planning data
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on cross-agent transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while Plane supports multiple instances but cannot write its filesystem and has no overlapping write scope documented. The pair therefore has limited direct write contention; any conflict would require an external shared resource not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external mutable resource
IF an operator grants Botpress write access outside its documented surfaces
mitigations: Keep Botpress and Plane on separate service accounts
Avoid sharing a mutable repo or directory between them
Use explicit locking on any external shared resource
requires-engineering: add resource-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress can generate support content that Plane may ingest through files, notes, or issue text, and Plane has broad egress plus API-calling surfaces. Without a documented verification step, Botpress output could be treated as authoritative and then propagated by Plane into downstream work products or communications.
conditions: IF Plane uses Botpress-generated text as the basis for issues, tasks, or outbound messages
IF no human verification occurs before Plane acts on Botpress output
mitigations: Require human approval before Plane acts on Botpress output
Mark Botpress outputs as unverified in Plane
Add a checklist to verify facts before ticket creation
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and gating
requires-engineering: separate draft generation from execution

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress and Plane are both open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, retention, or certification mismatch documented. The main compliance risk is operational: Plane stores files and notes, so if regulated data is routed through Botpress into Plane, retention and subject-rights handling may diverge, but this is not shown by the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Plane after being processed by Botpress
IF the operator relies on Plane retention settings without reviewing them
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared tickets
Review Plane retention settings before use
Document a deletion workflow for shared records
requires-engineering: align retention and export policies
requires-engineering: perform a residency/compliance review
